regions.title: Northern Rockies
regions.text: Grand Targhee is forecast for about 52". Jackson Hole and Big Sky follow.

regions.title: Cascades
regions.text: Mt. Bachelor is forecast for about 43". Crystal Mountain and Mt. Baker follow. The National Weather Service has rain mixed in at Crystal Mountain Thursday night.

regions.title: Coast Mountains
regions.text: Whistler is forecast for about 28". Cypress Mountain follows.

regions.title: Kootenays
regions.text: Whitewater is forecast for about 25", 15" of it Thursday. RED Mountain and Revelstoke follow.

regions.title: Central Rockies
regions.text: Steamboat is forecast for about 32", 24" of it Saturday. Vail and Arapahoe Basin follow.

regions.title: Tahoe
regions.text: Sugar Bowl is forecast for about 21", 13" of it Sunday. Palisades and Kirkwood follow. The National Weather Service has rain mixed in at Sugar Bowl Sunday and Sunday night.

regions.title: Wasatch
regions.text: Powder Mountain is forecast for about 19". Brighton and Solitude follow.

regions.title: Okanagan
regions.text: Big White is forecast for about 14", 10" of it Thursday. SilverStar and Sun Peaks follow.

regions.title: Northeast
regions.text: Mont-Sainte-Anne is forecast for about 8". Le Massif and Blue Mountain follow. Special Weather Statement at Mont-Sainte-Anne from Friday to Saturday.

regions.title: Eastern Sierra
regions.text: Mammoth is forecast for about 6", 5" of it Monday.

sources.name: NOAA buoys 51001 / 51101 (method: Powder Buoy, Mike Ruzek)

buoy.text: Buoys 51001 and 51101 near Hawaii popped Nov 25, the swell signal Powder Buoy watches for a Wasatch storm about two weeks later — here Dec 6–12. In past winters a pop raised the chance of a Wasatch storm in that window by roughly 6 to 12 points. Experimental: promising, not proven.
